pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #15
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

2. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agri- business Accounts? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Agri- business Accounts.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agri- business Accounts.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agri- business Accounts.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agri- business Accounts.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Erosion Control? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Erosion Control.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Erosion Control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Erosion Control.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Erosion Control.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Agricultural Biotechnology? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Agricultural Biotechnology.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Biotechnology.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Agricultural Biotechnology.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Agricultural Biotechnology.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Powered Agricultural Implements? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Powered Agricultural Implements.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Powered Agricultural Implements.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Powered Agricultural Implements.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Powered Agricultural Implements.

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

8. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. joule (J)
   D. newton (N)

9. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

10. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Producers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Breeding? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Breeding.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Breeding.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Breeding.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Breeding.

12. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 50 °C

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Livestock Nutrition and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Breeding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Animal Health: Disease Control and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

2. C — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

3. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agri- business Accounts.

4. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Erosion Control.

5. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Agricultural Biotechnology.

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Powered Agricultural Implements.

7. C — Glucose and oxygen

8. D — newton (N)

9. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

10. B — Producers

11. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Breeding.

12. A — 100 °C

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Livestock Nutrition; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Animal Breeding; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Animal Health: Disease Control; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
